t: What Consistency Model DB Internals Is All About
title: What Consistency Model DB Internals Is All About
description: The C in ACID: constraints, invariants, and keeping data valid under concurrency.. This database covers Consistency Model DB Internals with full records: definitions, key facts, working procedures, and runnable demo programs, arranged on a teaching ladder from Foundations to Advanced. ACID is a contract: atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability.
definition: Consistency Model DB Internals — The C in ACID: constraints, invariants, and keeping data valid under concurrency.
key_points: ACID is a contract: atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability.
Atomicity means all-or-nothing; undo logs implement it.
Durability means surviving crashes; WAL implements it.
Isolation is a spectrum; serializable is the top.
how_it_works: Define the transaction boundary: what must succeed or fail together?
Choose the isolation level: read-committed default, serializable for invariants.
Keep it short: do all reads, then writes, then commit; no user input inside.
Order lock acquisition consistently to prevent deadlocks.
Implement retry with backoff for serialization failures.
Test under concurrency, not just serially.
Monitor transaction age and lock waits in production.
Review: could this be smaller? Split if yes.

title: Declarative constraints

description: Application invariants. Rules like 'account balance never negative' live in transaction logic. The engine can't know them; tests and code review must. Property-based tests catch invariant violations that unit tests miss.

title: Consistency under concurrency
description: Consistency under concurrency. Constraints are checked against a transaction's snapshot plus its own writes. Unique checks need locking or predicate locks to be correct. This is why serializable is expensive: global validity needs global coordination.
definition: Consistency under concurrency — Constraints are checked against a transaction's snapshot plus its own writes.
key_points: Constraints are checked against a transaction's snapshot plus its own writes.
Unique checks need locking or predicate locks to be correct.
This is why serializable is expensive: global validity needs global coordination.
Deadlocks are prevented by lock ordering, cured by detection.
Optimistic concurrency validates at commit; good for low contention.
